testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: Verify branch is rebased on base (needs pull-request context and full git history, not the worktree); Validate renovate.json (fetches renovate from the npm registry via npx on every run); smoke-omp (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary); install-and-smoke (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary).

unverified.claim: The new check enforces only the ticket's required half: every `starting_cells` entry must be in `cells`. It does not enforce the optional half the ticket floated, that the Baseline Cell's starting set is a prefix of `cells`. So a fitted table whose `starting_cells` is a strict subset still validates when `cells` drops a starting Cell that was not recorded, and tableOver never produces such a table.
unverified.evidence: PR test (tests/ticket-router.test.mjs:893) asserts `bad({ cells: ["slow-medium", "task-high"], starting_cells: ["task-high"] })` is valid, and `node --test --test-name-pattern=validateTable tests/ticket-router.test.mjs` passed 4/4 in the copy. Probe: 70 tableOver outputs from fitTable/fitTree (5 baselines × all starting subsets) all validate, and every one has the full starting set first in `cells` (fitPulls' `[...set, ...drawn]`, ticket-router.mjs:815). The ticket marks the prefix check 'Optionally', and #4298 notes that a table may withdraw a starting Cell, so leaving it out is a defensible scope choice, not a bug.
unverified.suggested_fix: None needed for this ticket. If the stricter invariant is wanted, file it separately with a decision on the K=0 withdrawal case.

unverified.claim: No swallowed error, mislabelled catch or hidden fallback found in the new `starting_cells`-vs-`cells` check. `t.cells.includes` can't throw because the `cells` non-empty-array check runs earlier in validateTable and returns before this line. `sc?.find` runs only after `sc` has passed the Array check, so the optional chain skips nothing it shouldn't. The check returns an Error value outside any try.
unverified.evidence: Probe output: {cells:[slow-high], starting_cells:[slow-high,task-high]} -> "`starting_cells` names task-high, which `cells` does not hold"; starting_cells null, [] and "x" -> "`starting_cells` is not a non-empty list..."; cells null -> "`cells` is not a non-empty array". No TypeError in any case.

unverified.claim: Fits already on disk whose `starting_cells` names a Cell absent from `cells` are now refused, which is loud rather than silent. readFitBeside returns fallback "fit-invalid", which is surfaced as the routing REASON and shown as "Fit invalid: starting table" in compute-board. board-gather returns status "unreadable" with the validateTable message. The `fit:` step in metrics-refresh reports "fit: failed — <message>" if writeFit throws. Newly written Fits can't hit this because tableOver builds `cells` as [...set, ...drawn], and the starting set always covers `startingCells`.
unverified.evidence: Source read of readFitBeside (ticket-router.mjs ~L633-645), board-gather readRouterTable/readFit (stderr warnOnce, `why` in value), metrics-refresh fit() catch (say(`fit: failed — ${e.message}`)), and fitPulls' return of cells: [...set, ...drawn]. [INFERENCE] The tableOver/fitPulls claim is from source reading only; I did not run a fit end to end.

unverified.claim: No case has more than one starting Cell missing from `cells`, so which missing Cell the error names (first vs last) is not pinned.
unverified.evidence: red: n/a (survivor). Mutant `sc?.find(` → `sc?.findLast(` in plugin/scripts/ticket-router.mjs: `./agent-test --test-name-pattern="validateTable: each malformed" tests/ticket-router.test.mjs` → exit 0, tests 1 pass 1 fail 0 (survives); baseline same command → exit 0, test pass. The no-check mutant is killed: exit 1, tests 1 pass 0 fail 1, so the new check itself is covered.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a case such as cells: ["slow-medium"], starting_cells: ["slow-high","task-high"] expecting /names slow-high/.
